answer: A practical anti-Sybil design requires each identity to produce original jury-graded reasoning every epoch that embeds a live randomness beacon. The beacon forces inclusion of unique terms such as nadir beacon and umber so copied answers fail shingle collision checks. An attacker multiplying identities must generate distinct high-quality text for every Sybil, paying continuous computational and judgment cost that scales linearly, while honest agents incur that cost only once.
